title: reduce streaming token latency: refactor token loop, tune flush cadence, adaptive backpressure
author: Sofia Martinez
description:
Motivation: Streaming token generation latency had two persistent contributors: a tight token loop that introduced micro-scheduling overheads per-token, and suboptimal flush cadence + backpressure behavior that either increased tail latency or forced large flushes that hurt interactivity. This PR refactors the token emission loop, introduces an adaptive flush cadence heuristic, and adds a light-weight backpressure mechanism that interacts with the KV cache + continuous batcher to prioritize low-latency streams.

Changes in this PR: refactor token loop to avoid per-token allocation and reduce scheduler handoffs; add configurable flush cadence with adaptive mode based on observed throughput/latency; implement a token-emission backpressure token-bucket tied to KV cache hotness to avoid long GC/batch stalls; scheduler hinting to pin small low-latency streams to warm kernels (kernel pinning for low-seq paths); new unit and integration tests and benchmarks.

Checklist:
- [x] Token loop refactor (no per-token boxed closures, pooled buffers)
- [x] Adaptive flush cadence (config + runtime sampling)
- [x] Backpressure integration with KV cache and continuous batcher
- [x] Scheduler hints for kernel pinning of short/interactive streams
- [x] Benchmarks (microbench + service-level p50/p99)
- [x] Docs: streaming.md update and upgrade notes

Benchmarks (service-level, internal test harness, mixed workload representative of chat UX):
- baseline: p50 token latency 18.4ms, p95 72.1ms, p99 140.6ms
- this PR (adaptive mode enabled): p50 token latency 9.6ms (-48%), p95 39.8ms (-45%), p99 89.3ms (-36%)
- when running with heavy background batching workload, p99 tail reduced by ~30% compared to baseline.

Safety and rollout: change gated behind feature flag redwood.streaming.low_latency_opt. Default rollout to 10% traffic in staging for 48h, then progressive rollout with monitoring of token-level p99, KV cache miss rate, and batch utilization. Added an emergency toggle to revert adaptive mode without restart.

Related: ENG-4122 (streaming UX), ENG-4180 (kv-cache hotness metrics), SUP-872 (customer incident with tail latency on mixed workloads).

Notes: this PR focuses on runtime behavior and is non-breaking for API consumers. There are configuration knobs for teams that want to prefer throughput over single-token latency (e.g. continuous-batcher.max_batch_wait_ms).
